content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe the structure of the small intestine and villi
Explain how the structure of villi is adapted for absorption
Describe how different nutrients are absorbed
Explain the role of the large intestine in absorption

is the movement of digested food molecules from the gut into the blood. This mainly occurs in the small intestine, which has special adaptations to maximise the efficiency of absorption. The absorbed nutrients are then transported to cells throughout the body.
is the movement of small, soluble molecules from the intestine into the bloodstream (or lymph).
Large surface area for efficient absorption
Good blood supply to transport absorbed molecules
All nutrients (glucose, amino acids, fatty acids, vitamins, minerals, water)
Most absorption occurs in the small intestine.
